reviews.review:
Summary: Multiplayer Binding of Isaac as a side scroller
Multiplayer: Yes, 4p local and online co-op
Completion: 8 hrs
Cards: Yes
Cloud: Yes

Risk of Rain is a metroidvania of sorts, with many randomized features, but no procedurally generated levels. It's also pretty hard! There's no story in the traditional sense. Most of what's going on is mostly told through various backlogs or lore found on the planet, and even that is usually cryptic.

When starting the game you choose who your survivor is, and each has their own set of stats, powers and equipment. From there, you are thrown on the hostile alien planet, with everything out to get you, and now you must do your best to scavenge, survive, and to get off this crazy place.

Scattered throughout the land are a bunch of items. There's over 100 items that you can obtain, and interestingly, you can stack passive items. In a 1p game, you could be packing obscene amounts of gear. The game doesn't always provide a useful description for these items, and you usually can't tell what they do until you pick them up, but at least they are always beneficial.

The game has a lot of unlockable content. Throughout the game you may find various artifacts that once found become permanant toggles you can use each game from now on. Upon meeting certain conditions, you may also unlock new classes that all play differently. 

Somewhat unusual is the existence of the timer bar. As time goes on, enemies will become stronger whether you like them to or not. This scaling can be spotty, as on one level you might have little trouble, but on the next enemies are taking far too many hits. It's not a bad mechanic, but I would have liked it to stop once enemies were gone or at least slow down the progression.

Upon reaching a teleporter, a boss will appear, selected randomly, and you must surivive for a few minutes before you can take off. The bosses are pretty varied, whether they fly, burst from the ground, or just walk around. There's not a whole lot of them, however, and you can see repeats in a row. What bugs me most about the boss mechanic is that once it's defeated you must continue to exterminate all other critters in the area before you can evacuate.

One of the best features about the game is that it supports multiplayer. It's much more satisfying having a small squad going around covering your back, but to keep things somewhat balanced, items must be shared amongst everyone. If a player dies, they must wait until the next level to be automatically revived.

The graphics are all right, being low contrast pixel art. There's an awful lot of purples though, and with all the movings things on the screen it can get a little difficult to discern what's going on. The music's pretty good, being somewhat upbeat and alienish. I have not encountered any bugs or crashes, so that's always good.

I rate Risk of Rain a B-. The shooting aspect is fun, as is unlocking stuff, but the terrain does kind of get old after a while, and the continuous enemy scaling makes things pretty hard. The replayability is good, with all the available unlockables. As with most games, the game is more fun with friends, which this game does admirably, though having the share the fancy loot with others hurts a little. It's really impressive that the game was made by just two people, and I would like to see what they come up with in the future. Thanks for the copy, cc!
